title: Diatonic seventh harmony
description: Seven sevenths in major, natural-minor overview, and why the same 7 chord can have two jobs.

cards.front: What does diatonic harmony mean here?
cards.back: Chords built using only the notes of one key’s scale. Stack thirds on each degree and stay inside the scale.

cards.front: How are seventh Roman numerals written?
cards.back: Add 7 or maj7: V7, Imaj7, ii7. ° for diminished triads, ø for half-diminished sevenths (viiø7).

cards.front: List the seven seventh chords of C major with numerals.
cards.back: Imaj7 Cmaj7. ii7 Dm7. iii7 Em7. IVmaj7 Fmaj7. V7 G7. vi7 Am7. viiø7 Bm7♭5.

cards.front: What seventh-quality pattern appears in every major key?
Write the diatonic sevenths of G major.
cards.back: Gmaj7 Am7 Bm7 Cmaj7 D7 Em7 F♯m7♭5.

cards.front: Write diatonic triads and sevenths of D major and B♭ major.
cards.back: D: D Em F♯m G A Bm C♯° and Dmaj7 Em7 F♯m7 Gmaj7 A7 Bm7 C♯m7♭5. B♭: B♭ Cm Dm E♭ F Gm A° and B♭maj7 Cm7 Dm7 E♭maj7 F7 Gm7 Am7♭5.

cards.front: Write A natural minor’s diatonic triads and sevenths with numerals.
cards.back: i Am / Am7. ii° B° / Bm7♭5. III C / Cmaj7. iv Dm / Dm7. v Em / Em7. VI F / Fmaj7. VII G / G7.

cards.front: What does harmonic minor change on degree 5, and why?
cards.back: Raises 7 (G→G♯ in A minor) so degree 5 becomes E or E7. That restores a leading tone and a strong V to i. Typical cadence: i iv V7 i (Am Dm E7 Am).

cards.front: Should you memorize one fixed minor-chord list?
cards.back: No. Natural minor supplies the stable set, harmonic minor supplies major V, and melodic-minor ideas appear in melody and some chords.

cards.front: G7 is V7 in C major and VII7 in A natural minor. Same notes — same job?
cards.back: No. In C it pulls toward C. In A natural minor its natural pull is toward C (III), not Am. A dominant-seventh sound is not automatically the dominant of the key you are in.

cards.front: Give open-position seventh grips for C major I ii iii IV V vi viiø.
Play I vi ii V in C, then in G.
cards.back: C: Cmaj7 Am7 Dm7 G7. G: Gmaj7 Em7 Am7 D7.

cards.front: In G major, root at string 6 fret 3. Where are ii, iii, and IV along that string?
cards.back: A (ii, minor) fret 5, B (iii, minor) fret 7, C (IV, major) fret 8. Chords as a path along one string.

cards.front: In Am Dm E7 Am, which note of E7 is outside A natural minor?
cards.back: G♯, the raised 7 from harmonic minor.

cards.front: Play G7 to C and G7 to Am. Which resolves convincingly as a dominant, and why do the numerals differ?
cards.back: G7 to C is V7–I. G7 to Am is VII7–i and is weaker as a close. Same chord, different job in the key.
